page.layout: Two medallion woodcut portraits with their legends at top centre, below the running head. Below them one column of text running full width, with no marginal notes and no notes under the text.

main_text.p: CONSTANTIVS Chlorus & Galerius Maximinus fi-[?]tue Maximianus,ambo à Diocletiano & Maximiano Herculio, priusquâ se imperio abdicarent,Cæsares facti ac adoptati sunt, propter varia bella in diuersis locis pullulantia. Constátius natus patre Eutropio, qui genus ab Ænea deducebat, & matre Claudia,Claudii Augusti filia,Galliis,Hispaniis, Italiæ & Africæ præfuit:Galerius Illyrico,Græciæ & Orieti. At verò hac diuisione Imperii facta,Constantius natura mitis, & diuitiarum spretor,Italiæ & Africæ Imperiū recusat, quòd putaret ab vno tantū pōdus minimè sustineri posse:in Galliis & Hispaniis tantùm regnat,propensus ad promerendā Gallorum gratiam,nec à vera pietate abhorres.Vxores habuit duas,prior fuit Helena, ex qua Constantinū magnum suscepit:posterior fuit Theodora,priuigna Maximiani Herculii: quā dimissā Helena, coactus est ducere. obiit Constantius Eboraci, quod est oppidū in Britannia, anno 2. postquam Imperio se Diocletianus abdicauit: nam longè antea Cæsar factus,& à Diocletiano adoptatus fuerat.duos igitur veri Imperii annos Constátio tribuo,ab ipsa abdicatione Imperii à Diocletiano,quæ facta est an. mun. 4 2 6 9. à Christo nato 3 0 7. hoc regnante nulli motus in suis ditionibus extitere, hostes popu. Rom. ab armis cessauere. Dictus est Chlorus,à colore,quasi virens.Vide Pom.Læ.Egna.li.1.

HELENA, prior uxor Constantii,ac magni Constantini mater,annos nata 80.divinitus monita,Ierusalē perrexit: crucem in qua Christus pendit, non sine labore reperit: Romæ diem obiit,superstite filio, Deo hominibúsq; gratissima,anno mundi 4 2 8 6. à Christo nato 3 2 4. Vide Eusc. lib. 10. cap. 7. & Supple.Chro.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are printed inside the woodcut illustrations; the right-hand legend's final letters ("CON·MA·AV") are hard to read and are marked [?]. The word "fi-" at the line end of the first paragraph is uncertain (probably the start of "siue"), so it is marked [?]. The printed "Eusebius" abbreviation reads "Eufe." in the scan; it is transcribed as "Eusc." only if that is the correct reading, so treat "Eusc." with caution. The printed "Vide Eusc." may be a misreading of "Eufe." Printed spellings such as "Constátius", "Imperiū" and "pōdus" are kept as printed.
